This shop leads with 四色 at ¥2,000 — four soba in one order: さらし, 抹茶 (green tea), 胡麻 (sesame) and a seasonal one. Flavoured soba is made by working matcha, sesame or citrus peel into the dough, and because those additions weaken it the dough generally needs MORE binder, not less — so the coloured noodles a menu presents as the refined choice are, if anything, the more wheat-bearing ones. Nothing here publishes a ratio either way. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM IS BOTH NOODLES AT ONCE: うどん蕎麦合盛 at ¥1,200 serves soba and UDON on the same tray, which removes any doubt about wheat being in the kitchen. ⚠ THE PLATES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: 板わさ (¥1,200) is fish cake, which is a quiet wheat item; こんにゃく味噌田楽 (¥850) is konnyaku, a plant, under miso; アボカド山葵 (¥850) is avocado and wasabi and is the closest thing here to a clean plant dish; and 蕎麦がき at ¥2,000 is buckwheat paste rather than noodles, which is the one form of soba with no dusting flour on it — worth asking about even though the ratio question remains.

tokyo_vegan_eat_tokyo.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS THE ONLINE SHOP, NOT THE RESTAURANT BOARD — the stored website is a BASE storefront selling retort packs, so the four products below are what the shop mails out, not what it plates. No in-restaurant menu or price was found. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ AND IT CONTAINS THE SHARPEST SINGLE ILLUSTRATION OF THE TWO-AXIS PROBLEM IN THIS ENTIRE DATASET. The flagship product of a shop called VEGAN EAT TOKYO is its ヴィーガンカレー — and its own allergen line reads 小麦、カシューナッツ、大豆: WHEAT, cashew, soy. A vegan curry with wheat in it. Meanwhile the other product, ひよこ豆のトマト煮, is explicitly described as グルテンフリー. So within one vegan kitchen, the headline dish is closed to a coeliac and the second dish is open — and nothing about the word "vegan" predicts which. This is the asymmetry the dataset exists to record: plant-based is not wheat-free, the two restrictions are independent, and a shop can be scrupulous about one while the other is simply not the question it was answering. ⚠ THE CASHEW IS WORTH FLAGGING SEPARATELY: vegan kitchens use cashew constantly as a dairy substitute — for cream, cheese and sauce bodies — so a NUT allergy is a live and under-anticipated risk at exactly the restaurants a plant-eater is steered toward. It is named here in black and white.

It also notes that coffee and tea are served. Several lines are marked 期間限定 (limited season) or 数量限定 (limited quantity) and those markers are carried into the notes below, because a 5,500円 three-grape parfait that exists for a few weeks is not the same fact as a standing 1,400円 banana parfait. ⚠ A FRUIT PARLOUR LOOKS LIKE THE EASY CASE FOR BOTH DIETS AND IS NOT. A Japanese parfait is built in a glass in layers, and the layers under the fruit are the problem: whipped cream and ice cream are dairy in every one of these, and sponge, cornflake and wafer/biscuit layers are standard construction in this style of parfait. The shop does not publish a per-item build, so every line below is dairy — vegan 'no' — and every line is an open question on wheat rather than a safe one. ⚠ THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT THE FRUIT IS THE SAFE PART AND IT IS NOT SOLD SEPARATELY ON THIS PAGE; the parlour also runs a fruit counter and an online store, which is where an unassembled option would be, not here.

tokyo_abura_soba_kasugatei_shi.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE MENU IS A PICTURE. 油そば 春日亭's chain site has an お品書き page whose entire content is a single JPEG, images/contents/oshinagaki.jpg, with no alt text, no HTML list and no price anywhere in the markup. The only machine-readable sentence on it is an exclusion notice: 「※担々油そばに関しまして、魚介メニューの提供に伴い、中野店、神田店ではお取り扱いがございません」 — the tantan abura soba is not sold at the Nakano and Kanda branches because of their seafood menu. That footnote does NOT name 渋谷店 or 渋谷センター街店, so it does not restrict this shop. The chain lists 23 branches including both 渋谷店 and 渋谷センター街店. ⚠ WHAT IS CERTAIN WITHOUT READING THE IMAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE NAME OF THE SHOP: ABURA SOBA IS A WHEAT NOODLE. 油そば is a brothless ramen — thick wheat-and-kansui noodles tossed with a soy-and-oil tare at the bottom of the bowl — so every bowl on that card is wheat twice over, from the noodle and from the tare, and the 割スープ that is poured in at the end is a meat or fish stock. There is no version of this dish that is not wheat. Recorded empty for the prices; the gluten answer needs no image.

tokyo_nikujiru_suigyoza_gyopao_2.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE MENU IS A PICTURE, INCLUDING THE ENGLISH ONE. The branch's own site has four menu-ish pages — menu, course, 'Food & Drink / English edition' and an all-you-can-eat gyoza buffet page — and the English-edition page, which is the one that sounded most promising, turns out to be two scanned JPEGs of a printed card (grandmenu英語_page-0001.jpg and _page-0002.jpg) with no alt text and no HTML list behind them. No price appears in the markup of any page. Nothing has been transcribed and nothing invented. The branch is 肉汁水餃子 餃包 新宿東口駅前店, directly connected to Shinjuku Subnade, tel 050-1721-4408; its sister shop is KABUKI餃子. ⚠ WHAT THE PAGE STRUCTURE ITSELF ESTABLISHES: the headline offer is an ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT GYOZA BUFFET, and a gyoza wrapper is wheat by construction, so a coeliac has nothing to gain from the format that defines this restaurant. 水餃子 (boiled dumplings) are the house speciality and are wheat exactly as the pan-fried ones are; the 肉汁 in the name is the meat juice inside them. Recorded empty for the prices; the gluten answer needs no image. Worth returning to with OCR since a printed English card exists.

tokyo_trois_bagues_vertes.price_note: ALMOST EMPTY: THE SHOP'S SITE HAS NO MENU PAGE AT ALL. troisbagues.com's navigation is HOME / トロワバグについて / アクセス / ギャラリー / オンラインショップ / ブログ / お問い合わせ — there is no menu item in it, and the site even leaks a PHP warning (`Undefined variable $onepage_menu` in header-home.php) where a menu section would sit, which suggests the template once had one. No food or drink price appears anywhere. What the shop does publish about itself: a small 喫茶店 opened in 1976 (昭和51年) that ages its green beans before roasting — エイジングコーヒー, 熟成豆, オールドビーンズ — and brews by NEL DRIP; it offers a wine selection to taste, ships beans nationwide, and its gallery captions say 「軽食もございます」 (light meals are available) and 「ワインやビールもございます」 without naming a single one. It also runs a monthly wine gathering. 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-12-1 富田ビルB1, tel 03-3294-8597, one minute from Jimbocho A5; Mon–Fri 10:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:30), Sat and holidays 12:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:30), closed Sundays. ⚠ ONLY ONE PRODUCT IS NAMED ANYWHERE ON THE SITE — トロワブレンド, the house blend built on its old beans — and it is named in the ONLINE SHOP block, i.e. as a bag of beans to buy rather than as a cup served at the counter. It is recorded below on that basis and unpriced, which is why this record is provisional/low. ⚠ THE 軽食 IS THE REAL GAP: a Showa-era kissaten's light meals are toast, sandwiches, pilaf and spaghetti nearly without exception, all of which would be wheat, but the shop names none of them and that must not be filled in from the pattern.

items.note: The only product named anywhere on the site: the house blend built on the shop's aged old beans, brewed by nel drip at the counter and also sold as beans through the online shop. Black coffee has no wheat and no animal ingredient in itself; whether it is served that way, and what the shop's unnamed 軽食 are, is not published. No price given.
